All existing scripts in `.github/scripts/` are used as-is.\n\n---\n\n## Review Dimensions §1–§13\n\n**Standards:** UEFI 2.10+, PI 1.8+, EDK II C Coding Standard 2.2+\n\nThese 13 review dimensions and 4 Abort Trigger gates govern per-CC code evaluation in Stage 2 Phase B. Each dimension is an ordered review gate evaluated sequentially.\n\n---\n\n### Dimension Applicability by File Type\n\n| Priority | File types | Applicable dimensions |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | SMM/StandaloneMM/SecureBoot/Crypto `.c`/`.h` | §1 (all triggers) · §2–§11 · §12 |\n| P2 | Standard DXE/PEI/Runtime `.c`/`.h` | §1 (all triggers) · §2–§11 · §12 |\n| P3 | `.inf`/`.dsc`/`.fdf`/`.dec` | §1 (Triggers #8, #12, #18 only) · §13 |\n| P4 | `.sdl`/`.mak`/`.cif`/`.veb` | §1 (Trigger #8 only) · §13 |\n| P4 | `.asl` | §1 (Trigger #12 if EDK2-owned) · §13 |\n| P4 | `.nasm`/`.asm` | §1 (Triggers #1, #2, #3, #15, #16 for SMM paths) · §13 |\n| P5 | `.vfr`/`.sd`/`.uni` | §13 only |\n| P6/P7 | Test/docs/scripts | §12 (copyright/`@file` only) |\n| P8 | Binary | No review (`[➡️ BINARY]`) |\n\n---\n\n### §1. Abort Trigger Gates (check FIRST)\n\nApply trigger groups in order. Skip a group if it does not apply to the current module type, file type, or changed hunk — note the skip only when it materially affected review scope. Any confirmed match produces **🛑 BLOCK** and must be recorded as `[🛑 CRITICAL – ABORT TRIGGER]`.\n\n#### Gate A — SMM Isolation and Lock-Window\n\n**Applies when:** file is SMM-related by MODULE_TYPE, path, library usage, or changed handler registration logic.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 1 | SMRAM address/pointer as return value or `OUT` param to a non-SMM caller |\n| 2 | `LocateProtocol`, `HandleProtocol`, or `gBS->` call inside an SMM handler body |\n| 3 | CommBuffer pointer or size field written back to DXE-accessible memory by an SMM handler without sanitization — return-oriented data leak |\n| 15 | SMM handler or child dispatch handle registration (`Register`, `SmmRegisterProtocolNotify`, `InstallProtocolInterface`, or `SmmInstallProtocolInterface` for child protocols such as `EFI_SMM_SW_DISPATCH2_PROTOCOL`) after `EFI_SMM_READY_TO_LOCK_PROTOCOL` installed — covers both direct handler and child-dispatch lock bypass |\n| 16 | `AllocatePages` for SMRAM-resident code without configuring NX attributes via `EFI_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTES_PROTOCOL` — leaves SMM code pages executable, enabling code-injection if SMRAM is writable |\n\n#### Gate A-MM — Standalone MM Isolation\n\n**Applies when:** MODULE_TYPE = `MM_STANDALONE` or `MM_CORE_STANDALONE` or path contains `StandaloneMm/`, `MmStandalone/`, or `Standalone/`.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| MM-1 | `gSmst->` (traditional SMM services table) used inside a Standalone MM module — must use `gMmst->` (`EFI_MM_SYSTEM_TABLE`) instead; direct `gSmst->` access from `MM_STANDALONE` is an architectural violation = CRITICAL |\n| MM-2 | `EFI_MM_COMMUNICATE` CommBuffer dereferenced using `SmmCommunicateHeader.MessageLength` instead of `MmCommunicateHeader.MessageLength` — wrong header struct for Standalone MM path = MAJOR |\n| MM-3 | MM handler or child dispatch handle registered after `EFI_MM_READY_TO_LOCK_PROTOCOL` installed — same lock-window violation as Trigger #15, applied to Standalone MM context = CRITICAL |\n| MM-4 | `gBS->` or any Boot Services pointer accessed inside a Standalone MM handler — Boot Services are unavailable in Standalone MM execution context = CRITICAL |\n| MM-5 | `AllocatePages` for MMRAM-resident code without configuring NX attributes via `EFI_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTES_PROTOCOL` — leaves MM code pages executable, enabling code-injection if MMRAM is writable = CRITICAL |\n| MM-6 | `gMmst->MmLocateProtocol()` or `gMmst->MmHandleProtocol()` output pointer dereferenced without first verifying return is `EFI_SUCCESS` — null-protocol dereference inside Standalone MM handler = MAJOR |\n\n> **Gate A vs Gate A-MM:** Apply Gate A for `DXE_SMM_DRIVER`/`SMM_CORE`. Apply Gate A-MM for `MM_STANDALONE`/`MM_CORE_STANDALONE`. When MODULE_TYPE is unresolved and both SMM and Standalone MM are plausible, apply both gates and record `[DUAL-GATE-APPLIED: A + A-MM — MODULE_TYPE unresolved]`. When dual-gate fires produce overlapping findings on the **same line**, merge into a single finding citing both violations: `[DUAL-GATE: Gate A Trigger #N + Gate A-MM Trigger MM-N]`; severity is CRITICAL regardless. Do not emit two separate findings for the same line. **A dual-gate merged finding counts as ONE CRITICAL for Agent State, scoring, and verdict Rows 2–4 regardless of how many triggers contributed.**\n\n#### Gate B — CommBuffer and Untrusted-Size\n\n**Applies when:** changed code reads CommBuffer fields, dispatch contexts, DMA buffers, or untrusted size arithmetic.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 4 | `CopyMem`/`SetMem`/array write where length comes from external input with no bounds check |\n| 5 | CommBuffer, DMA buffer, or dispatch pointer dereferenced before size/NULL check |\n| 6 | CommBuffer cast or field-index without `≥ sizeof` guard — **(a)** SW SMI handler casts `DispatchContext`/CommBuffer without checking `MessageLength ≥ sizeof(struct)`; **(b)** `SmmCommunicateHeader.MessageLength` used to cast or index CommBuffer without a `≥ sizeof` guard — apply whichever sub-point matches; never fire both on the same line |\n| 11 | `+`/`*`/`<<` on untrusted values fed to `CopyMem`/`SetMem`/`AllocatePool` size without SafeIntLib |\n| 17 | SMM handler reads CommBuffer fields a second time after initial validation instead of using an SMRAM-local copy — CommBuffer must be copied to an SMRAM-local struct before any code path that performs a **functional** field access (i.e., any access that influences control flow, output, or memory operations); non-functional reads inside `DEBUG()` macros are exempt when the module is not built with debug output in the release configuration; any subsequent functional field access that reads from the original DXE-accessible pointer is a TOCTOU exploit |\n\n> **Overlap note — CommBuffer family (#5, #6, #17):** Apply the most specific trigger only; never stack multiple triggers on the same line:\n> - **#5** — pointer/size dereferenced *before* any NULL/size check\n> - **#6** — cast or indexed without `≥ sizeof` guard\n> - **#17** — re-reads CommBuffer fields after validation instead of using the SMRAM-local copy\n\n#### Gate C — Runtime, S3, and Authenticated-Variable\n\n**Applies when:** changed code touches runtime callbacks, S3 boot script logic, or security database variables.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 7 | `gBS->` call inside `ExitBootServices` callback or `DXE_RUNTIME_DRIVER` after `SetVirtualAddressMap`. **Also flag** `FreePool()`, `FreePages()`, or `FreeBuffer()` (MemoryAllocationLib wrappers or direct `gBS->` form) called inside an `ExitBootServices` callback — Boot Services memory management is unavailable at this point; calling these APIs causes unpredictable exceptions — CRITICAL. Detection: function registered via `CreateEventEx()` with `gEfiEventExitBootServicesGuid` or `CreateEvent(EVT_SIGNAL_EXIT_BOOT_SERVICES, ...)` whose body contains `FreePool`, `FreePages`, or `FreeBuffer` |\n| 10 | `EFI_S3_SAVE_STATE_PROTOCOL.Write()` called after `EndOfDxe`, or target region writable by DXE |\n| 13 | `SetVariable` to `db`/`dbx`/`dbt` (`EFI_IMAGE_SECURITY_DATABASE*`) without `EFI_VARIABLE_TIME_BASED_AUTHENTICATED_WRITE_ACCESS` attribute — bypasses image security database authentication |\n| 14 | `EFI_S3_SAVE_STATE_PROTOCOL` callback registration or `.Write()` call inside a `DXE_RUNTIME_DRIVER` or after `SmmReadyToLock` notification — S3 boot-script window violation |\n\n#### Gate D — Build, Ownership, and Image-Policy\n\n**Applies when:** patch changes SDL/build configuration, upstream-owned code, or image verification flow.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 8 | `KEYS_DIR` or `DEBUG_MODE` token patched — follow chain to confirm the unsafe state: test keys still enabled in a release build (`DEBUG_MODE = 0`) |\n| 9 | Image verification returns `EFI_SUCCESS` unconditionally or skips signature check |\n| 12 | File under `Intel/`, `MdePkg/`, `MdeModulePkg/`, `SecurityPkg/`, `CryptoPkg/`, `StandaloneMmPkg/`, or `UefiCpuPkg/` modified without an AMI OVERRIDE marker. **Accepted syntax (any of the following is valid — do NOT fire if any variant is present):** For `.c`/`.h`: (1) `// AMI OVERRIDE START/END`, (2) `//APTIOV_OVERRIDE_START/END`, (3) `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_START:/END:`, (4) `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_START:/END:`, (5) any `//` comment matching regex `(AMI\\|APTIOV)[A-Z_]*OVERRIDE[A-Z_]*START`. For `.inf`/`.dec`/`.dsc`/`.fdf`/`.mak`/`.cif`: same patterns with `#` comment prefix. Fire **only** when the changed hunk contains **no** override marker of any accepted variant. **AMI copyright banner exemption:** When a file is classified as ⚙️ **Third-party with AMI overrides** (file contains BOTH third-party and AMI copyright), the AMI copyright block itself (lines matching `Copyright.*AMI` or `//***` banner pattern) does NOT require wrapping in override markers — do NOT fire Trigger #12 for a hunk consisting solely of AMI copyright banner lines, provided at least one correctly-formed override block exists elsewhere in the same file. If the AMI copyright banner is the ONLY change in the file with no override markers anywhere → fire Trigger #12 (copyright-only change with zero markers = stealth modification). |\n| 18 | `InstallProtocolInterface` or `InstallMultipleProtocolInterfaces` targeting `gEfiSecurityArchProtocolGuid` or `gEfiSecurity2ArchProtocolGuid` in a `DXE_DRIVER` outside `SecurityPkg/`. Exception: designated security handlers in `SecurityPkg/` or `AmiSecureBootPkg/` are exempt |\n\n**On match:** mark `[🛑 CRITICAL – ABORT TRIGGER]` and continue reviewing remaining CCs.\n\n**Trigger #8 evaluation chain:** (1) patched value → (2) project `.sdl` → (3) `CrbPkg/*.sdl` → (4) `AmiPkg/Configuration/Configuration.sdl`. Fire only when the unsafe combination is confirmed: test keys selected while `DEBUG_MODE = 0` (release build). If PCD cache marks the token `[BUILD-TIME-ONLY]`, rely exclusively on the SDL chain walk. If also unresolvable, emit `[TRIGGER-8-UNRESOLVABLE]` as INFO — do NOT block.\n\n> Abort Triggers (#1–#18) are fully evaluated through Gates A–D. Dimensions §2–§13 must NOT re-evaluate any Abort Trigger pattern. If a dimension check overlaps with a trigger, skip it — the trigger verdict stands.\n\n---\n\n### §2. Security\n\n- `BootOrder`/`BootXXXX` NV writes without auth check = MAJOR when Secure Boot path reachable\n- New GUIDs: collision check performed in Step 2.2 mandatory GUID uniqueness check\n- Keys/passwords must not appear in `DEBUG()` args = MAJOR\n- DMA buffers in protected memory; IOMMU/VT-d enabled before DMA access — missing = CRITICAL\n- `gBS->LocateProtocol()`, `gBS->OpenProtocol()`, `gBS->HandleProtocol()` output pointer dereferenced without first verifying return is `EFI_SUCCESS` = MAJOR (null-protocol dereference)\n- `LocatePpi()`/`GetPpiList()` output pointer used without `EFI_SUCCESS` check in PEI context = MAJOR\n\n### §3. Memory Safety\n\n- **`ExitBootServices` callback — `FreePool`/`FreePages`/`FreeBuffer` forbidden:** These APIs must not be called inside an `ExitBootServices` callback (`EVT_SIGNAL_EXIT_BOOT_SERVICES` / `gEfiEventExitBootServicesGuid`). Boot Services are unavailable at this point; calling memory-free APIs causes unpredictable exceptions — CRITICAL. Memory no longer needed after boot must be freed **before** `ExitBootServices` fires. **Agent must never suggest adding `FreePool`/`FreePages`/`FreeBuffer` inside an EBS callback as a fix.** If the lifecycle check below finds a missing free whose only plausible placement is inside the EBS callback, close as `FALSE POSITIVE` — do not open a finding.\n- Every `AllocatePool`/`AllocatePages` has matching `FreePool`/`FreePages` on all exit paths — missing = MAJOR. **EBS exception:** if the only location where the free is absent is an `ExitBootServices` callback body, treat as `FALSE POSITIVE` per rule above — never suggest adding the free call there.\n- No use-after-free, no dangling pointers, no protocol pointers held across uninstall — violation = CRITICAL\n- **`CR()`/`BASE_CR()` macro cast without Signature guard** — cast recovering outer struct via `CR()`/`BASE_CR()` must verify `Struct->Signature == EXPECTED_SIGNATURE` immediately before or after the macro; missing guard = MAJOR when the pointer is externally supplied or crosses a trust boundary (e.g., originating from a protocol caller, CommBuffer, or DXE↔SMM interface); missing guard = MINOR-A when the pointer originates from the module's own protocol installation and no external attacker path exists; if SMM-resident struct with DXE-accessible pointer origin = CRITICAL\n- No unsafe string APIs (`StrCpy`/`AsciiStrCpy`/`sprintf`) — use safe `*S` equivalents = MAJOR\n- `AsciiSPrint`/`UnicodeSPrint`/`AsciiVSPrint`/`UnicodeVSPrint`: `BufferSize` from untrusted arithmetic without SafeIntLib = MAJOR\n- Credential/key buffers zeroed with `ZeroMem` before `FreePool` — missing = MAJOR if buffer held password, key, or auth token\n- Local stack arrays > 4 KB in SMM or Standalone MM (`MM_STANDALONE`) = MAJOR\n- `GetVariable()` return checked `EFI_SUCCESS` before arithmetic on `DataSize` — using `DataSize` after failure = MAJOR\n- `GetVariable()` two-pass size pattern: verify (a) `DataSize > 0` before allocation and (b) second call returns `EFI_SUCCESS` before buffer dereference — either missing = MAJOR. *Cross-check:* if the variable is security-sensitive, also verify §4 `VariableLock->RequestToLock()` is present\n- **API migration — double pointer OUT parameters:** When `AllocatePool`/`AllocateZeroPool`/`AllocatePages`/`AllocateRuntimePool` replaces `gBS->AllocatePool(Type, Size, &Buffer)`, verify correct dereference: `VOID **OutputParam` → must write `*OutputParam = AllocatePool(...)` and check `*OutputParam == NULL`. Assigning to the local parameter copy leaves the caller's pointer unchanged = CRITICAL (memory leak + uninitialized pointer dereference)\n- **API migration — mixed allocation/deallocation APIs:** MemoryAllocationLib allocation paired with `gBS->FreePool`/`gBS->FreePages` = MAJOR. Correct pairings: MemoryAllocationLib → `FreePool`/`FreePages`; Boot Services → `gBS->FreePool`/`gBS->FreePages`. Partial migration in progress → flag as MAJOR with recommendation to complete consistently\n- **String pointer storage in struct members:** Struct members of type `CHAR8 *`, `CHAR16 *`, or `char *` assigned from allocated buffers must either (a) copy the string data with `AllocateCopyPool`/`AllocateZeroPool` + `AsciiStrCpyS`/`StrCpyS` or (b) transfer ownership by nulling the source pointer after assignment. Pattern: `Context->StringPtr = AllocatedBuffer; FreePool(AllocatedBuffer);` without prior copy = CRITICAL (dangling pointer). Correct patterns: (1) `Context->StringPtr = AllocateCopyPool(AsciiStrSize(Src), Src); FreePool(Src);` or (2) `Context->StringPtr = Src; Src = NULL;` (ownership transfer). Verify the stored pointer is freed in the struct's cleanup/destructor function; missing cleanup = MAJOR (memory leak)\n- **String pointer array cleanup:** For arrays like `CHAR8 *StringSet[]` or `CHAR16 *StringArray[]`, ownership must be explicit. If strings are heap-allocated copies (via `AllocateCopyPool`, `AllocatePool` + `StrCpyS`, or `StrDuplicate`-like helpers), each element must be freed individually in a loop before freeing the array itself: `for (i = 0; i < Count; i++) { FreePool(StringArray[i]); } FreePool(StringArray);` — missing per-element free = MAJOR (memory leak). If strings are borrowed references (pointers to static strings, .rodata, or external buffers not owned by this module), freeing individual elements = CRITICAL (use-after-free / double-free). Detection heuristic: trace string assignment origin — if from `AllocatePool`/`AllocateCopyPool`/`StrDuplicate`, ownership transferred; if from string literal, global buffer, or function returning `CONST CHAR*`, borrowed reference. Ambiguous cases → `Confidence: MEDIUM` with recommendation to document ownership contract\n\n### §4. Variable Service Security\n\n- Security-sensitive NV variables locked via `VariableLock->RequestToLock()` before `EndOfDxe` — missing = MAJOR\n- `GetVariable()` single-call with hardcoded buffer on untrusted variable = MAJOR (two-pass pattern → §3)\n- `EFI_VARIABLE_AUTHENTICATION_2`: `AuthInfo.Hdr.wCertificateType` must be `WIN_CERT_TYPE_EFI_GUID` — writing without valid descriptor = MAJOR\n- `EFI_VARIABLE_NON_VOLATILE + RUNTIME_ACCESS` audited for necessity; large NV write without `QueryVariableInfo` = MINOR\n\n### §5. S3 Resume Security\n\n- Pointers passed to `Write()` must not be stack variables or DXE-writable ACPI NVS buffers — violation = MAJOR\n- Hardware writes to TSEG/SMRR registers must be immediately followed by a lock step — missing = MAJOR\n\n### §6. Concurrency & Locking\n\n- `EFI_LOCK`: `EfiInitializeLock` before first use; every `EfiAcquireLock` has matching `EfiReleaseLock` — missing release = MAJOR\n- SMM: `SmmAcquireLock`/`SmmReleaseLock` around shared globals from multiple CPUs/APs — unprotected = MAJOR\n- Standalone MM (`MM_STANDALONE`): `SmmAcquireLock`/`SmmReleaseLock` are not available; use `EFI_SPIN_LOCK` (via `SynchronizationLib`) to protect shared globals accessed by MM handlers from multiple APs — unprotected `= MAJOR`\n- `EFI_SPIN_LOCK`: `InitializeSpinLock` before use; `AcquireSpinLock`/`ReleaseSpinLock` balanced — unbalanced = MAJOR\n- TPL: raising to lower TPL than current = MAJOR; `TPL_HIGH_LEVEL` outside interrupt context = MAJOR\n- `EFI_MM_MP_PROTOCOL.DispatchProcedure()`: shared globals from AP procedures must be guarded by `EFI_SPIN_LOCK` — unprotected = MAJOR (PI 1.8 §4.10.2)\n\n### §7. Spec Compliance (UEFI 2.10+ / PI 1.8+)\n\n- `[UEFI]` UEFI types only (`EFI_STATUS`, `UINTN`, `UINT8/16/32/64`, `BOOLEAN`, `VOID`, `EFI_HANDLE`) — no `int`/`char`/`void` = MINOR\n- `[UEFI]` `gRT->` callable post-`ExitBootServices` — runtime-safe memory only = MAJOR\n- `[UEFI]` Protocols installed/uninstalled properly (pointer lifetime → §3)\n- `[UEFI]` Variable services: proper attributes, size validated, GUID traceable (`EFI_STATUS` checking → §8)\n- `[PI]` PEI: PPIs only, no protocols; CAR limits apply; no temp RAM pointers in HOBs\n- `[PI]` DXE: `[Depex]` lists all required protocols/GUIDs\n- `[PI]` SMM: SMRAM locked after `SmmReadyToLock`; CommBuffers validated\n- `[PI]` Standalone MM (`MM_STANDALONE`): MMRAM locked after `EFI_MM_READY_TO_LOCK_PROTOCOL` installed; CommBuffers validated using `EFI_MM_COMMUNICATE_HEADER`; `gBS->` and all Boot Services unavailable; `gSmst->` must not be used — use `gMmst->` (`EFI_MM_SYSTEM_TABLE`) exclusively\n- `[PI]` HOBs: `GET_GUID_HOB_DATA_SIZE >= sizeof(<Type>)` validated by DXE consumers\n- `[PI]` Phase separation: PEI must not use DXE-only interfaces; runtime must not use boot-only interfaces\n\n### §8. Correctness & Lifecycle\n\n- Every `EFI_STATUS` return checked — not silently discarded = MAJOR\n- All error paths clean: no leaked resources, no held mutexes — violation = MAJOR\n- All `else`/`default` branches handle errors = MINOR — **FP guard:** before flagging, confirm the branch is not an intentional fallback path (e.g., a by-design default return or NO-OP documented in comments); if intent is by design, classify as INFO or skip\n- Re-entrancy guards for functions callable from nested events — missing = MAJOR\n- TPL safety: shared data at `TPL_APPLICATION` protected by TPL raise — unprotected = MAJOR\n- Every `CreateEvent`/`CreateEventEx` matched by `CloseEvent` on non-success paths and in `Stop()`/unload — missing = MAJOR\n- `ExitBootServices` callback must not call `gBS->`, `AllocatePool`, or `FreePool` — violation = MAJOR\n- `OpenProtocol(BY_DRIVER)` in `Start()` matched by `CloseProtocol()` in `Stop()` — mismatch = MAJOR\n- Buffers from `AppendDevicePath`/`DuplicateDevicePath` freed with `FreePool` on all exit paths — missing = MAJOR\n\n### §9. PEI-Specific Depth\n\n- Local arrays > 1 KB in any PEI function = MAJOR (CAR stack ~64–128 KB; risks overflow)\n- Pre-memory `AllocatePool` results must not be referenced after `MemoryDiscoveredPpiNotify` — stale reference = MAJOR\n- `BuildGuidDataHob` size must equal `sizeof(<struct>)` exactly — over/under = MAJOR\n- `BuildGuidDataHob` alignment: if struct natural alignment ≥ 8 bytes and `sizeof(struct)` is not a multiple, HOB data area is not naturally aligned for X64 consumer casts — undefined behavior = MAJOR\n- `GetFirstGuidHob()` result NULL-checked; `GET_GUID_HOB_DATA_SIZE` validated ≥ `sizeof(expected struct)` before cast — missing = MAJOR\n- `PeiServicesGetBootMode()` consulted before S3/recovery-specific init = MINOR\n\n### §10. Capsule / FMP Security\n\n- `LowestSupportedImageVersion` honored; any bypass = CRITICAL (anti-rollback)\n- `CheckImage()` return gated before `SetImage()` — `SetImage()` without prior success = MAJOR\n- `UpdateImageTypeId` matched against `GetImageInfo()` `ImageTypeId` — silent mismatch = MAJOR\n- Capsule payload size validated against actual buffer length before parsing — missing = MAJOR\n- `CAPSULE_FLAGS_PERSIST_ACROSS_RESET` set only when reset is required — otherwise = MINOR\n\n### §11. General Algorithmic & Functional Logic\n\nReview functional correctness of changed `.c`/`.h` code independent of UEFI/PI spec mandates. Apply Pre-Finding Gate before opening any finding. Findings here are typically MINOR unless they cause data corruption or incorrect control flow affecting firmware reliability. Tag findings `[LOGIC]`.\n\n> **§8 / §11 tie-breaker:** If a correctness issue also involves `EFI_STATUS` semantics, protocol lifetime, event/lock balance, or resource lifecycle, classify it under §8 (Correctness & Lifecycle) and do not duplicate it under §11.\n\n- **Off-by-one errors:** Loop bounds (`<` vs `<=`), buffer index, array sizing — incorrect bound = MAJOR if buffer accessed\n- **Inverted or wrong condition:** `==` vs `!=`, `>` vs `>=`, negated flag, wrong enum in `switch`/`if` — causes incorrect branch = MAJOR\n- **Dead / unreachable code:** `return`/`break`/unconditional assignment renders subsequent lines unreachable — MINOR; if it masks error path = MAJOR — **FP guard:** an explicit early-return guard (e.g., `if (Ptr == NULL) { return EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER; }`) or a documented intentional fallback is not dead code; do NOT flag it even if the happy path always executes after it\n- **Stale or wrong variable used:** Copy-paste error with wrong variable — MAJOR if data corruption results\n- **Incorrect bit manipulation:** Wrong shift, missing mask, bit cleared instead of set — MAJOR if affects hardware register or security flag; MINOR otherwise\n- **State machine correctness:** Missing transition, unreachable terminal state, skipped required intermediate — MAJOR if firmware stalls or mis-sequences init\n- **Integer wrap / truncation (non-security):** Narrowing cast or decrement below zero on `UINTN`/`UINT32` — MINOR if no security path; MAJOR if controls allocation or copy\n- **Redundant or contradictory logic:** Condition always true/false, duplicate `if` branches — MINOR\n- **Incorrect return value:** Returns value not matching documented contract — MAJOR\n- **Uninitialized variable used:** Local variable read before assignment on some code path — MAJOR if influences control flow or output\n- **Algorithm correctness:** Sorting/searching/checksum/table-walk loops: verify algorithm matches stated intent — MAJOR if incorrect result silently propagates\n- **Preprocessor conditional scope violation:** A variable, label, or function *defined* inside an `#if`/`#ifdef`/`#ifndef` block but *referenced* outside the enclosing `#endif` — causes a compilation error when the condition is not met = MAJOR `[LOGIC]`. Detection: when a diff hunk introduces a symbol definition inside a conditional block, `grep_search` the file for uses of that symbol name outside the enclosing `#if`/`#endif` pair; if found → MAJOR. **FP guard:** if the same symbol is also declared or defined unconditionally elsewhere in the file (e.g., a guard-free fallback declaration), do NOT flag.\n\n### §12. EDK II C Coding Standard 2.2+\n\n- **Naming:** PascalCase functions · `g` prefix globals · ALL_CAPS macros/constants = MINOR\n- **Indentation:** 2 spaces per level; no tabs = MINOR\n- **Comments:** Doxygen `/** ... **/` for file/function docs; `//` inline = MINOR\n- **No implicit fall-through** in `switch` — end each `case` with `break`, `return`, or `// FALL THROUGH` = MINOR; if it masks a security branch = MAJOR\n- **Magic numbers:** named `#define` macros only = MINOR\n- **ASSERT:** via `DebugLib`; never sole security gate (stripped by `MDEPKG_NDEBUG`) = MAJOR. A **sole security gate** means `ASSERT()` is the only check preventing an unsafe operation — e.g., `ASSERT(Buffer != NULL)` immediately before `CopyMem(Dst, Buffer, Size)` with no prior `if (Buffer == NULL) return;` runtime guard. ASSERTs protecting internal invariants structurally unreachable from external attacker-controlled input are not security gates; classify those as INFO.\n- **Parameter qualifiers:** `CONST`/`IN`/`OUT`/`IN OUT` match actual usage; `IN` param must not be modified = MINOR\n- **Copyright year** ≥ commit year; `@file` block present = INFO\n- **Include order:** `<Uefi.h>` or `<Pei.h>` first, then `<Token.h>`, AMI libs, EDK2 libs, protocols, platform headers = INFO\n- **Code Organization & Placement** — review only high-signal structural cases. Aggregate into single `[🔷 MINOR-B]` finding tagged `[CODE-ORG-AGGREGATE]`:\n   - Function prototypes/declarations mid-file (after first `{`) = MINOR `[CODE-ORG]`\n   - `#include` directives not at file top (after `#define`/`typedef`/`struct`/`extern`/function body) = MINOR `[CODE-ORG]`\n   - Global variable declarations after first function definition = MINOR `[CODE-ORG]`\n   - All other placement issues: better handled by linting/CI unless they hide a security guard or cause build error\n- **INF section rules:** see §13 for `[Packages]` ordering, section validation, and DSC cross-check\n\n### §13. File-Type Specific (non-`.c`/`.h` files only)\n\n#### `.inf` files\n\n- `[Defines]` complete · `[Sources]` lists changed files · `[Packages]` MdePkg first\n- `[LibraryClasses]`/`[Protocols]`/`[Ppis]`/`[Guids]` match actual usage (cross-check DSC) — **FP guard for section classification:** before flagging a GUID identifier as in the wrong section, read the owning package `.dec` file to confirm its declaration section (`[Protocols]`, `[Ppis]`, or `[Guids]`); the INF section must match the `.dec` declaration — do NOT rely on naming conventions alone; if `.dec` is inaccessible, tag `[INF-SECTION-UNVERIFIED]` and downgrade to INFO\n- `[Depex]` covers all required protocols and notify-install callbacks\n- `[Pcd]`/`[PcdEx]` entries match actual usage — before flagging an entry as unused, apply the two-step check:\n  - Step 1: grep the module's `.c` source for `PcdGet*()`/`PcdSet*()` on that PCD name\n  - Step 2: if Step 1 returns no matches, **grep the headers transitively included by the module** for `_PCD_VALUE_<PcdName>` or `_PCD_SIZE_<PcdName>` — EDK2 emits these as compile-time array-dimension constants into `AutoGen.h` only when the PCD is declared in `[Pcd]`; a header expression such as `UINT32 Table[_PCD_VALUE_PcdFoo]` is a valid passive consumer that mandates the `[Pcd]` entry\n  - If Step 2 finds a match → `FALSE POSITIVE`; do NOT open a finding. Only flag unused when **both** steps return no matches.\n- INF-DELTA mismatches from Stage 1 cache: apply the three-tier severity as defined in Step 3.1.7 (CRITICAL → security-critical; MAJOR → default; MINOR → call path unreachable)\n\n#### `.sdl` files\n\n> 📖 **SDL skill — load on demand only:** When `SDL-TOKEN`, `SDL-ELINK`, `SDL-MODULE`, `SDL-PCDMAP`, or `SDL-LIBMAP` CCs are present in the Stage 1 registry, load the `/sdl-handling` skill (`.github/skills/sdl-handling/SKILL.md`) for authoritative Aptio V field names, syntax rules, validation checks, and DSC/FDF translation tables. **Do not load this skill when no SDL CCs are registered — it is not needed and increases review time unnecessarily.**\n\n**Authoritative Aptio V field names (skill is the source of truth — these override the SDL spec document names):**\n\n| Object | Correct field name in Aptio V SDL | Spec-doc alias — appears only in NDA field tables, NOT in real SDL; do NOT require this name in submitted code and do NOT flag submitted code that uses the correct left-column name |\n|--------|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `INFComponent` | `ModuleTypes` (plural) | `Module_Type` |\n| `LIBRARYMAPPING` | `ModuleTypes` (plural) | `Module_Type` |\n| `PcdMapping` | `GuidSpace` | `Guid` |\n| `PcdMapping` | `PcdType` (full `\"Pcds\"` prefix required) | `Pcd_Type` |\n| `PcdMapping` | `DataType` | `Data_Type` |\n| `FFS_FILE` | `Apriori_Index` must be a quoted string | bare integer |\n\n**False positive guards — do NOT open findings for these valid Aptio V SDL patterns:**\n\n| Pattern observed | Correct interpretation — not a defect |\n|-----------------|---------------------------------------|\n| Multiple `Token = \"A\" \"=\" \"1\"` lines on one SDL object | AND-logic multi-condition — not a duplicate field violation |\n| Two `PcdMapping` blocks sharing the same `Name` but inverse `Token` conditions | Valid else-branch pattern — not a TOKEN uniqueness or duplicate-block violation |\n| `FFS_FILE` block with no `Module_Type` field | `Module_Type` is **mutually exclusive** with `INFComponent`, `File_Stmt`, and `OpRom` per NDA spec — when `INFComponent` is present (normal Aptio V case), `Module_Type` must be absent; do NOT flag this absence as a missing required field |\n| `LIBRARYMAPPING` `Instance = \"Pkg.ComponentName\"` dot format | Required format — not a path error |\n\n- TOKEN uniqueness and correct override layer · PcdMapping type/guards correct · MODULE path valid · `INFComponent.Name` unique across all SDL files · `INFComponent.File` path relative to Package root\n- LibraryMapping `Class` / `Instance` (`\"Package.ComponentName\"` dot format) / `ModuleTypes` correct\n- ELINK: no duplicate Name+Parent; missing trailing comma on function-name entry = MAJOR (hard build error); verify return type + param types against cached prototype\n  - Confirmed signature mismatch = MAJOR; escalate to CRITICAL when hook runs in security-boundary-sensitive path — determined by chain name keywords (`Smm`/`StandaloneMm`/`SecureBoot`/`Auth`/`Capsule`) **or** registered function's MODULE_TYPE being `DXE_SMM_DRIVER`, `SMM_CORE`, `MM_STANDALONE`, `MM_CORE_STANDALONE`, `DXE_RUNTIME_DRIVER` or similar\n  - `VOID*`↔typed-pointer = MAJOR\n  - Typedef not found = MINOR — `[ELINK-PROTOTYPE-UNVERIFIED: manual build verification required]`\n- `DISABLE_CAPSULE_AUTHENTICATION=1` = MAJOR · `SDL_REGRESSION` entries = MAJOR\n- For `KEYS_DIR` / `DEBUG_MODE` TOKEN changes: apply Trigger #8 (§1 Gate D)\n- Security-sensitive ELINK chains: verify hook does not bypass upstream security\n- **TOKEN rename or removal — consumer dependency check:** When a diff deletes a `TOKEN` block or changes a TOKEN `Name` field, extract the old name from the removed diff lines (`-    Name  = \"OLD_TOKEN_NAME\"`). Run `grep_search` workspace-wide across `.c`, `.h`, `.sdl`, `.mak`, and `.asl` files for the old token name. Consumers to detect: `#if OLD_TOKEN_NAME`, `#ifdef OLD_TOKEN_NAME`, `defined(OLD_TOKEN_NAME)`, `$(OLD_TOKEN_NAME)` in `.mak`/`.sdl` `Value` fields, `Token = \"OLD_TOKEN_NAME\"` SDL conditions. **Any match = MAJOR** — the old name is still consumed; a rename without a global update causes consumers to silently evaluate to `0` (undefined macro = 0 in the C preprocessor) or fail SDL dependency resolution with no compile error, making it a silent behavioral regression. No consumers found → PASS. Tag `[TOKEN-DEPENDENCY: <N> consumer(s) found — <file:line list>]` or `[TOKEN-DEPENDENCY: CLEAR — no consumers of old name detected]`.\n- **ELINK chain-root rename or removal — orphan child check:** When a diff deletes or renames an ELINK that has no `Parent` field (`InvokeOrder = ReplaceParent` — a chain root), extract the old `Name` value. Run `grep_search` in `.sdl` files for `Parent  = \"<old-name>\"`. Also check `.c` files for the old generated macro name (typically `<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE_OF_NAME>` used in `extern` or array declarations). **Any match = MAJOR** — child ELINK entries point to a non-existent root; the SDL build tool generates an empty or broken dispatch list, silently dropping all registered hooks. Tag `[ELINK-ROOT-ORPHAN: <N> child(ren) still reference old root \"<old-name>\"]`.\n- **ELINK leaf-entry removal — hook removal check:** When a diff removes an ELINK that has a `Parent` field (a leaf/contributor entry registering a function into a chain), verify the removed hook is not the sole registered entry for a security-sensitive chain (keywords in chain name: `Smm`, `StandaloneMm`, `SecureBoot`, `Auth`, `Capsule`, `Password`, `Key`). Sole security hook removed → **MAJOR**. Non-security or non-sole hook removed → **MINOR-A**. Tag `[ELINK-HOOK-REMOVED: <function-name> unregistered from chain \"<parent-name>\"]`.\n\n#### `.dec` files\n\n- `[Defines]` complete · `[Includes]` paths valid · GUID/PCD entries unique = MAJOR\n\n#### `.fdf` files\n\n- FV names match DSC · no region overlap · `AmiTrustedFvPkg` boundaries intact · security modules in correct FV\n- Boundary or security-module violation = CRITICAL; other = MAJOR\n\n#### `.vfr`/`.sd`/`.uni` files\n\n- Varstore type/size matches C struct · Question IDs unique = MAJOR · INTERACTIVE+callback pairing correct = MAJOR\n- No orphaned `suppressif` · Security options not inadvertently hidden = MAJOR · String tokens present in `.uni` = MINOR\n- `efivarstore` binding: verify `VariableLock->RequestToLock()` exists before `EndOfDxe` — missing lock = MAJOR when the variable carries `RUNTIME_ACCESS` attribute or contains security-sensitive data (boot order, auth tokens, keys); missing lock = MINOR-A when the variable lacks `RUNTIME_ACCESS` and is a non-security HII staging buffer whose writes are confined to the boot-services phase; verify backing variable uses `EFI_VARIABLE_NON_VOLATILE` — volatile-backed varstore silently loses data on warm reset = MAJOR\n\n#### `.asl` files\n\n- `_STA` bits 5–31 not set = MINOR\n- `OperationRegion` field access width matches field alignment — mismatch = MAJOR\n- `_OSC` input `Buffer` ≥ 16 bytes; undersized dereference = MAJOR\n- `Notify()` opcode validated for device type; out-of-range = MINOR\n- `_PRS` end-tag present; `_CRS` buffer size consistent with descriptor list — truncated = MAJOR\n- No hardcoded MMIO/PCI addresses conflicting with bridge `_CRS` or DRHD entries = MAJOR\n- `_DSM` implementation: `Arg2` (function index) range-checked before dispatch; `Arg3` (function-argument package) structure validated before element access — missing validation = MAJOR; `Arg0` (UUID buffer) matched against the expected GUID before any `_DSM` handler is invoked — missing UUID check allows wrong-handler invocation = MAJOR\n- `OperationRegion` field `AccessType` must be compatible with the field's `BitOffset` and `BitLength` — e.g., `ByteAcc` field with `BitOffset` not on an 8-bit boundary, or `WordAcc` without 16-bit alignment = MAJOR\n- `Notify()` target device must be defined and reachable within the current ASL namespace scope — referencing an undefined or out-of-scope device node = MAJOR\n\n#### `.nasm`/`.asm` files\n\n- Stack alignment preserved per x64/IA32 calling convention (16-byte for x64, 4-byte for IA32) — misalignment = MAJOR\n- Callee-saved registers (RBX, RBP, RDI, RSI, R12-R15) preserved across function calls — missing preservation = MAJOR\n- For SMM entry/handler code (`SmiEntry`, `SmiException`, `*Smm*.nasm`): no `gBS->` or Boot Services calls — CRITICAL (§1 Trigger #2); SMRAM pointers not leaked to non-SMM code — CRITICAL (§1 Trigger #1); handler registered after `ReadyToLock` — CRITICAL (§1 Trigger #15)\n- Control-flow integrity: RET instructions paired with CALL; no arbitrary JMP to computed addresses without validation — unpaired = MAJOR\n- Interrupt flag (`CLI`/`STI`) manipulation justified and paired — unbalanced = MAJOR for SMM/exception handlers\n- Memory operand sizes match declared data types — size mismatch = MAJOR\n- CET (Control-flow Enforcement Technology) compliance when `CET_ENABLED`: shadow stack operations correct; ENDBR64/ENDBR32 present at indirect call targets — missing = MINOR when CET disabled; MAJOR when CET enabled per INF `[Defines]` or build flags\n- For S3 resume code: temporary stack usage bounds-checked; no persistent pointers to CAR/temp memory stored in HOBs or variables — unbounded stack = MAJOR\n\n#### `.veb` files\n\nThe `.veb` file is the project manifest that maps every `.cif` component to its source-control label. Each entry has the format:\n`\"<path>.cif\"= \"SS: AptioV;$/<source-path>;<ModuleName>_<LabelNumber>\"`\nThe label is the last `;`-delimited token. Multiple `.cif` entries for the same module share the same label. Skip any entry whose value is `Private`.\n\n**Case 1 — Commit message consistency:** Collect all added `+` diff lines. Extract each unique module label suffix (text after the last `;`, e.g. `NvmeRstPassword_11`). Parse the commit message for those label identifiers. Any changed label that is **not mentioned** anywhere in the commit message → **MAJOR**. Tag `[VEB-LABEL-COMMIT: <N> unexpected entries changed — <list of unmentioned labels>]`. If all changed labels are covered → PASS.\n\n> **Multi-module sync commits:** A commit that bumps multiple packages (e.g., Intel RC sync) must list every changed label in the commit message. Unlisted labels still fire MAJOR.\n\n**Case 2 — SDL version token match:** For each unique changed module label:\n1. Determine the package SDL — e.g., `NvmeRstPassword_11` → `AmiChipsetModulePkg/SB/NvmeRstPassword/NvmeRstPassword.sdl`; `AmiTrustedFvPkg_22` → `AmiTrustedFvPkg/AmiTrustedFvPkg.sdl`. Use the `.cif` path prefix to locate the owning SDL.\n2. `grep_search` the package SDL for any TOKEN block with `_VERSION` or `_REVISION` in its Name and a `Value` field.\n3. **Compare:** Extract the numeric label suffix from the `.veb` entry (e.g., `11` from `NvmeRstPassword_11`). Compare with the token `Value`.\n   - **Match → PASS.** Tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: CONSISTENT — <TOKEN_NAME> = <value>]`.\n   - **Mismatch → MAJOR.** Tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: MISMATCH — .veb label <N> but <TOKEN_NAME> = <M>]`.\n   - **False-positive guard:** If the token name ends in `_REVISION` (not `_VERSION`) **and** the token's Help text contains a cross-reference note mapping revision to label (e.g., `\"Rev59 = SVN label 55\"` or `\"Rev<X> = label<Y>\"`), then a numeric difference between the label and the token value is **intentional and documented**. In this case downgrade to **INFORMATIONAL** and tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: REVISION-OFFSET-NOTED — Help text documents deliberate offset; label <N>, token <TOKEN_NAME> = <M>]`. Do NOT fire MAJOR.\n   - **No version token found → INFORMATIONAL.** Tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: NO-TOKEN — no _VERSION or _REVISION SDL token found in <sdl-path>]`. This is expected for Intel RC packages (e.g., `RaptorLakePlatSamplePkg`, `ClientOneSiliconPkg`) which use composite version strings and have no integer SDL token.\n   - **Complex label strings** (e.g., `RaptorLakePlatSamplePkg_0C.00.43.42(7113.00)_066`) — no integer SDL token is expected; skip Case 2 and emit `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: NO-TOKEN — Intel RC composite label, no SDL token expected]`.\n\n#### `.dsc`/`.mak`/`.cif`/`.nsh` files\n\n- Copyright year (see §12) · general correctness only\n- For `.dsc` `[PcdsFixedAtBuild]` hunks: if `PcdCpuSmmRestrictedMemoryAccess` is present, confirm it is not `FALSE` in a release build (`DEBUG_MODE = 0`) — raise MAJOR\n"
